analysis.title: Market Intelligence: US Morning Update (27 October 2026)
key_insights: Asia was mixed on Tuesday. Korea rose over 1% after 3Q26 GDP accelerated to +1.0% from +0.6% a quarter earlier. China fell about 1% after industrial profits were unchanged.
European equities are slightly lower in early trading. French consumer confidence came in weaker than expected. GS describes cross-asset price action as 'refreshingly benign'.

Hatzius (Global Views, 10/26): global growth has been 'remarkably unremarkable' this year, with fiscal easing and AI offsetting drags from energy and tariffs. A similar pace is expected in 2027, with increasing downside risks.
Hatzius's listed downside risks: energy prices back near March/April highs, DM yields up about 100bp since 2026, AI's growth impulse peaking, and potential labor-market disruption.
Hatzius expects fewer rate hikes than are currently priced in, and expects the S&P 500 to resume gains after the US midterm elections.

Mehta (Oil & Gas E&P): oil E&Ps are well positioned even at long-term WTI of $70-75/bbl. GS anchors coverage to a $73/bbl mid-cycle WTI price and sees a 12% average 2027/28 FCF yield. Highlighted Buys are PR, DVN and OXY (OXY is on the Conviction List).

Energy M&A: EQT announced an all-stock acquisition of RRC at over $50B combined enterprise value, creating the largest natural gas producer and marketing platform. OVV announced an all-cash acquisition of Logan Energy for US$890M (C$1.26B).

Healthcare is in focus around ESMO. JNJ management outlined an ambitious prostate cancer strategy built on potentially practice-changing data, with prostate as the first proof of concept for the RIPTAC platform.

MRK expressed optimism that partner Kelun's China-based sac-TMT trials will translate to MRK's global Ph3 trials. It also expressed confidence in combining intismeran with Keytruda across multiple tumor types after a positive melanoma readout.

In lung cancer, a KOL viewed AMGN's Imdelltra in small cell lung cancer as the most practice-changing ESMO readout, with a major overall survival benefit. The KOL was also encouraged by MRK/Kelun data that replaces chemotherapy with an antibody drug in one form of lung cancer.

AAPL reports next Monday. Mike Ng expects in-line fiscal F4Q26 results: iPhone revenue +15% y/y, Services +10%, gross margin 47.8%. Supply constraints and memory cost pressure are near-term headwinds, while recent price increases on iPhone, Mac and iPad should support December-quarter revenue and margins.

For fiscal 2027, GS sees AAPL growth from iPhone 18 pricing, iPhone Duo replacement demand, spring launches, easier supply compares and Services expansion. Hardware elasticity and App Store monetization remain key debates.

Hasbro (HAS, Buy, 12m PT $126): GS sees durable growth in Magic: The Gathering from collectibles demand, Universes Beyond, distribution growth, ARPU upside and a new digital platform over 2-3 years. Watch the video game strategy and profitability and licensing focus.
TKO (Buy) reports Nov-4. GS expects a 3Q revenue beat but an EBITDA miss on weaker WWE revenue and margin. 12m PT cut to $215 from $220. The key item is an update on remaining Middle East events.
FWONK (Buy) reports Nov-5. GS expects beats on F1 segment revenue and OIBDA on sponsorship strength. 12m PT cut to $116 from $117.
Today's US data: durable goods, Case-Shiller, Conference Board consumer confidence and new home sales. Many companies report before the open, including BA, UPS, KO, PYPL, SPGI, FCX and HCA.
GS rating changes: Weg SA upgraded to Buy from Neutral; Gjensidige cut to Neutral from Buy; Richful cut to Neutral from Buy; Sumitomo Bakelite initiated at Buy.

Other notes listed: PM reiterated Buy as a top stock idea; VZ 3Q26 beat and raise but service revenue missed; JBLU 3Q behind consensus with a better-than-expected 4Q revenue outlook; Vale 2H26-2027 earnings downgrade; CDNS strong guidance.
GS Housing Market Activity Scale for the week of Oct 18 fell to 3 as purchase applications and sales declined, despite modest relief in rates.
